subject: [Status] Elevated 503s for /v1/generate in us-east-1 — ops bridge and mitigation
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alison Nguyen <alison.nguyen@peninsulahealth.org>, techops@peninsulahealth.org
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:05 -0400
Subject: [Status] Elevated 503s for /v1/generate in us-east-1 — ops bridge and mitigation

Hi Alison and team,

We're seeing elevated 503 responses for the hosted /v1/generate endpoint in the us-east-1 cluster that is servicing your integration. This started around 08:50 EDT and is affecting a subset of requests with longer context lengths (customer-side sequences > 1k tokens). Our SREs are on an active ops bridge and we're running two mitigation steps now:

- Routing traffic away from the impacted host pool to adjacent capacity in us-east-2 (in-progress).
- Temporarily lowering max sequence length for new requests to avoid a pathological KV cache allocation path (deploying in the next 10m).

We will update you every 30 minutes on progress. If you see anything on your side (spikes in 5xx or degraded responses), please reply and include timestamps; that helps our correlation.

Apologies for the disruption — I know Peninsula Health has critical workflows running. We're treating this as P1.

Attachments: incident_log_us_east_0422.txt (excerpt), error-sample-0422.json

Best,
Irene Choi
Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:40:31 -0400
Subject: Re: [Status] Elevated 503s for /v1/generate in us-east-1 — ops bridge and mitigation

On Thu, 22 Apr 2027 at 09:12, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We're seeing elevated 503 responses for the hosted /v1/generate endpoint in the us-east-1 cluster...

Quick update from SRE: we observed memory pressure on a specific serving pool (gpu-serve-pool-7) that caused worker processes to drop requests with 503 before queueing. The routing shift to us-east-2 is live for ~3m; early indicators show a ~60% reduction in 503 rate for routed traffic.

Next steps underway:
- Rolling restart of gpu-serve-pool-7 with an updated kernel to avoid the KV cache growth path (ETA 25m).
- Enable temporary request-size throttling for tenants that exceed 1k token context to limit amplification while the restart completes.

I'll keep the bridge attached and post logs here. (attachment: incident_log_us_east_0422.txt)

—Ben
Ben Carter
SRE — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 16:03:10 -04:00
Subject: Post-incident update and next steps — us-east-1 503s (April 22)

Alison and team,

Thank you for your patience. This is a consolidated post-incident update following the P1 on Thu 2027-04-22. High-level summary:

What happened
- Starting ~08:50 EDT a serving pool (gpu-serve-pool-7) in us-east-1 started returning elevated 503s for longer-context requests due to an unforeseen KV cache growth interaction with a specific kernel path.

Impact
- Peninsula Health experienced increased 503s for ~28 minutes; routed traffic to us-east-2 recovered ~60% of traffic immediately. Some in-flight requests failed and need resend logic on your side to preserve ordering.

Resolution steps completed
- Traffic rerouted to adjacent capacity (us-east-2).
- Rolling restart and kernel patch applied to gpu-serve-pool-7.
- Temporary per-tenant context throttling removed after stability validated.

Follow-ups for Redwood (we own these)
- Formal postmortem draft (link below) and root cause analysis: INF-8421.
- Backfill of request-level retry guidance for customers (technical note and SDK snippet).
- Add automated early-warning metric for KV cache slope to prevent recurrence.

Actions for Peninsula Health
- Please replay the failed request window (08:48–09:05 EDT). We have preserved trace IDs in the attached incident_log_us_east_0422.txt and can provide a filtered list on request. If you need assistance with safe resubmission to maintain order, Marissa can coordinate with your engineering team.

Links & artifacts
- Public incident entry: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-04-22-us-east-503s
- Postmortem draft (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-incident-assets-peninsula
- JIRA ticket: INF-8421

Attachments: postmortem-draft-peninsula-0424.docx

If you'd like a 30m sync to walk through logs and the resubmit pattern, Marissa and I are available tomorrow morning EST.

Thanks again — we'll follow up when the internal postmortem is finalized.

Best,
Irene Choi
Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
